articles.title: AI First
articles.rule: Use AI to analyse, explain and recommend while preserving human control.

articles.title: Configuration over Hardcoding
articles.rule: Business rules must originate from configuration or explicit contracts.

articles.title: Behaviour before Components
articles.rule: Validate complete behaviour chains, including forbidden outcomes.

articles.title: Human Approval for Risk
articles.rule: High-impact actions require explicit human approval.

articles.title: Explainability Required
articles.rule: Every automated verdict must include reason and evidence.

articles.title: Registered Capabilities
articles.rule: Every platform capability must be registered with owner and dependencies.

articles.title: Contracted Behaviour
articles.rule: Every user-visible capability must have a behaviour contract.

articles.title: Release Integrity
articles.rule: Every release must prove feature, impact and platform consistency.

articles.title: Controlled Complexity
articles.rule: Complexity increases require justification and registered technical debt.

articles.title: No Vendor Lock-in
articles.rule: Features request capabilities and must not depend directly on a specific AI provider.

articles.title: Shared Experience Context
articles.rule: Channels and touchpoints share one governed experience context rather than isolated silos.

articles.title: Industry-neutral Core
articles.rule: Platform Core must remain independent of any specific industry, tenant, customer or experience.

articles.title: Domain Isolation
articles.rule: Industry-specific logic belongs in domain packs above Platform Core.

articles.title: Contract-first Data
articles.rule: Important platform data must use versioned, traceable, privacy-aware and transport-neutral canonical contracts.

articles.title: Shared Context by Contract
articles.rule: Cross-channel context must be purpose-bound, minimal, expiring and contract-based. Persistent identity or personal data requires explicit policy and approval.

articles.title: Evidence before approval
articles.principle: A release may only be approved when the promised behaviour has observable evidence at every required test level. Missing evidence is not a pass.
articles.enforcement: Verification Governance derives mandatory test suites from capability profiles and blocks incomplete evidence.

articles.title: Human-Governed AI
articles.rule: AI may observe, analyse, recommend, implement and verify only within explicit risk policies; strategic, high-impact or irreversible actions require human approval.

articles.title: Continuous Measured Improvement
articles.rule: Improvements must progress from evidence through verification and measurement before the platform records learning or claims impact.

articles.title: Governed Actions
articles.rule: Every platform action must use the canonical action contract, carry evidence and verification, and obey risk-based human approval before execution.

articles.title: Evidence before interpretation
articles.principle: AI may interpret observations, but it may not be treated as the primary source of facts. User-facing conclusions must be traceable to verified evidence and their confidence may not exceed evidence quality.
